text:
maria: thinking out loud — the current continuous-batcher admits everything into the single coalesce window and we end up jittering latency for small tenants. what if we add a lightweight gate that keeps tiny-requests on a fastpath until they exceed a shaping budget?
kevin: sounds reasonable. by 'shaping budget' you mean token-count per tenant per second, or something more nuanced?
maria: token-count is a start but i want it to consider deadline-hints and request size. e.g., two 16-token requests vs one 512-token request should be treated differently.
jamal: +1. also: how does gate interact with the KV cache warmup? if we fastpath too many small requests we could miss cache hits for larger sequences and hurt throughput.
erin: maybe two-tier gating: "fast-path" for tiny, latency-sensitive requests, and "warmup-path" for mid-size requests that are eligible for batching but still need preferential treatment. both governed by per-tenant credits.
maria: agreed. sketching rough rules here:
```
# gate config proto (toy)
fastpath.max_tokens = 32
fastpath.rate_limit_per_tenant = 100 reqs/min
warmup.min_tokens = 33
warmup.max_tokens = 256
warmup.credit_window = 10s
```
This is just a thought — credit_window lets us allow bursts while still steering large flows into the normal coalesce.
kevin: what about interface boundaries? i think gate should be a pure admission decision: return ADMIT_FASTPATH | ADMIT_WARMUP | DEFER_TO_BATCHER. the scheduler then makes decisions without peeking into tenant logic. keeps code modular.
jamal: yes, admission enums are nice. but we need metrics for each path and reasons (e.g., "exceeded fastpath rate", "kv-warmup requested"). otherwise debugging will be painful.
erin: also add a fallback: if fastpath GPUS are saturated we should downgrade to DEFER_TO_BATCHER automatically. ops-bot can emit alerts when saturation crosses threshold.
ops-bot: alert: fastpath-saturation at 78% on pool gw-03 — consider scaling or increasing warmup credits. (auto note)
maria: on rollout strategy: start with the gate off, then enable fastpath but cap to 1% of traffic per box, ramp to 10%, evaluate latency tail and KV hit impact. A/B with canary tenants.
kevin: good. thoughts on config surface? per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers? or just tenant-class (free/paid/enterprise) + feature flags?
jamal: per-tenant overrides are heavyweight. prefer tenant-class with opt-in per-tenant flags for a small set of skus (e.g., 'latency-sensitive'). keep defaults global to avoid explosion.
erin: make sure rollout has a kill-switch at routing layer too; if something breaks, we can route all traffic to the legacy batcher.
maria: compatibility note: the gate must not change request semantics. admission decisions are only about scheduling; responses and logs unchanged. Also persist gate telemetry to the same tracing span for correlation.
kevin: can we add a lightweight sim-mode metric that counts "would-fastpath" decisions so we can run traffic through the decision logic without affecting production?
maria: yes — add sim-mode flag that increments telemetry but returns DEFER_TO_BATCHER. we'll run that for 48h on broad traffic before flipping.
jamal: finally, long-term: consider replacing hard thresholds with a small policy model that predicts if admitting now increases tail latency beyond tenant SLO. but let's get deterministic gates first.
erin: agreed. next steps: maria to draft an RFC with the admission enums, proto config, rollout plan and metrics. kevin/jamal to review perf sims. i'll hook ops-bot to the canary alerts.
maria: i'll write the RFC draft by EOD Friday and include a csv of sim-mode results from last week. thanks all. :tada:
